briefs.headline: Mac Allister's father says Liverpool have not opened renewal talks
briefs.summary: Carlos Mac Allister told ESPN in an interview published Friday that there have been no contract renewal talks between Liverpool and his son, that 20 months remain on the midfielder's deal, that the sporting director and the head coach have both changed and the situation is under review, and that there may be news before the end of the year; Alexis Mac Allister, 27, said in September he had not been offered a new deal in the summer and chose to stay, has started every Premier League match under Andoni Iraola with one league goal and three in the Champions League, and his father said the family is talking only about Liverpool, the club that signed him from Brighton in 2023.

briefs.headline: Bengals meet the Steelers for the AFC North lead with the NFL's worst run defense
briefs.summary: Cincinnati and Pittsburgh are tied atop the division going into Sunday's 8:20 p.m. ET game at Paycor Stadium, the seventh time the two have met with first place in the AFC North at stake, and the winner took the division in five of the previous six, per AP's preview; Joe Burrow leads the league in completion rate, passing yards per game and touchdown passes, with at least three in each of the four straight wins, while the Bengals rank 25th against the run at an NFL-high 5.04 yards per carry and face Jaylen Warren, whose 5.92 yards a carry lead the league and who had 176 yards from scrimmage in the Steelers' September win in Pittsburgh. Pittsburgh comes off a bye and may get receiver Michael Pittman back from a four-week foot injury; Cincinnati played Atlanta in Madrid last Sunday, and teams off a bye have won all five such games against an opponent returning from an international date.

briefs.headline: De La Cruz finishes 4th in the NL MVP vote won unanimously by Crow-Armstrong
briefs.summary: Elly De La Cruz placed fourth in the National League Most Valuable Player voting the BBWAA announced Thursday night, with 173 points, behind the Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong, who took all 30 first-place votes and 420 points, the Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani (264) and the Brewers' Brice Turang (190); Sal Stewart was the other Reds player named, with four points, and the Pirates' Brandon Lowe was the only Pittsburgh player on a ballot, with six points, per the BBWAA's full table. The MLB Stats API transaction log for Nov. 12 and 13, read at 5:47 a.m. ET Friday, lists no move for either club.

briefs.headline: Verse says he met with the Browns' psychiatrist to break a sackless slump
briefs.summary: Jared Verse said Thursday in Berea that he recently met with the team psychiatrist and that his problem is a mental block, not a physical one, after nine games in Cleveland without a sack since the trade that sent Myles Garrett to the Rams; NFL Next Gen Stats lists him as one of three players with at least 200 pass-rush snaps and no sack this season, his pressure rate ranks 180th of 199 qualifiers and his edge win rate 55th of 56, per ESPN, and Todd Monken said last week that comparing him to Garrett was always unfair and that the sacks would come as the Browns play from ahead. Houston, whose Will Anderson Jr. leads the NFL with 9.5 sacks against a Cleveland line that has allowed a league-high 38, visits Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Spurs host the Warriors tonight without Curry, out 2 weeks with an oblique tear
briefs.summary: Stephen Curry will miss at least two weeks with an oblique abdominal tear, and sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Thursday that Golden State is bracing for closer to a month; the injury rules him out of the Warriors' next seven games, starting with tonight's 9:30 p.m. ET NBA Cup group game at the Frost Bank Center against a San Antonio side that has won 10 straight and sits half a game behind the Lakers at the top of the West. Curry, averaging 27.8 points in 26.3 minutes on a career-best 45.7% from 3-point range, was hurt in the first quarter of Wednesday's loss in Houston that ended Golden State's eight-game run; Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody are already out with knee injuries, and Steve Kerr said the concern is high.

briefs.headline: Pochettino agrees a United deal and will coach both Haiti legs first, sources say
briefs.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become Manchester United's manager on a two-and-a-half-year contract, with an announcement expected Friday, sources told ESPN early Friday; the sources said he has a deal with U.S. Soccer to take charge of Saturday's 4:30 p.m. ET first leg in Miami and Tuesday's 7 p.m. ET second leg in Cincinnati before traveling to Manchester, where United expect him at Carrington on Wednesday ahead of Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22, and that chief executive Omar Berrada told the federation Wednesday the club would trigger the $10 million release clause in the extension he signed in August. Separately, U.S. Soccer said Thursday that defender Sergino Dest, who arrived in camp with a minor injury, leaves Friday as a precaution and returns to PSV, trimming the roster to 24.

briefs.headline: West Virginia beats Mercer 75-61 with a 12-3 run to open the second half
briefs.summary: Finley Bizjack scored 15 points, hit a 3-pointer at the buzzer for a 31-28 halftime lead after Mercer's 11-2 surge had tied it at 28, and made all five of his free throws, Miles Sadler and Javan Buchanan added 12 apiece, and the Mountaineers, 10 of 32 from the floor and 4 of 18 from distance before the break, shot 50% in the second half at Hope Coliseum on Thursday night in the first meeting between the schools; Shane Cherry scored 20 and Karon Boyd had 10 points and eight rebounds for Mercer, per AP. West Virginia, 3-0, plays Auburn in the Players Era 8 in Las Vegas on Tuesday.

standings.line: Chelsea are 5th in the Premier League on 16 points from 10 matches (5 wins, 1 draw, 4 losses, GD +3), level on points with 6th-place Everton and two behind 4th-place Liverpool (18), per the ESPN standings page read at 5:48 a.m. ET Friday, unchanged with the league paused for the international break; Arsenal lead on 27, Brighton are 2nd on 22 and Manchester City 3rd on 21. Chelsea next host Leeds, 9th on 14, on Saturday, Nov. 21.

Liverpool are 4th in the Premier League on 18 points from 10 matches (5 wins, 3 draws, 2 losses, GD +4), nine behind leaders Arsenal (27) and three behind 3rd-place Manchester City (21), per the ESPN standings page read at 5:48 a.m. ET Friday, unchanged through the international break; Manchester United, their Nov. 22 visitors to Anfield and the club Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to join per ESPN's sources, are 18th on 8.

Tottenham are 11th in the Premier League on 12 points from 10 matches (3 wins, 3 draws, 4 losses, GD -1), level on points with 12th-place Newcastle and one behind 10th-place Aston Villa (13), per the ESPN standings page read at 5:48 a.m. ET Friday, unchanged through the international break; Ipswich, Tottenham's Nov. 21 visitors, are 14th on 11.

The Bengals are 6-2 (W4), level on record with Pittsburgh (6-2, W4) in the AFC North, which ESPN lists first with Cincinnati 2nd, Cleveland 5-4 and Baltimore 4-5, and listed as the AFC's 6th seed with the Steelers 4th, per the ESPN NFL standings page read at 5:48 a.m. ET Friday, unchanged with the division idle since Monday night; Buffalo (7-1) holds the 1st seed and Denver (7-2) the 2nd. The Steelers visit Cincinnati on Sunday night.

The Browns are 5-4 (L2), 3rd in the AFC North, 1.5 games back of Pittsburgh and Cincinnati (both 6-2) and a game ahead of Baltimore (4-5, L4), and listed as the AFC's 8th seed, one place outside the seven-team playoff line behind 7th-seeded New England (5-4), per the ESPN NFL standings page read at 5:48 a.m. ET Friday, unchanged; Sunday's visitors Houston are 3-5 (W1), 2nd in the AFC South, three games behind Jacksonville (6-2).

FC Cincinnati finished 9th in the MLS Eastern Conference on 46 points from 34 matches (12 wins, 10 draws, 12 losses, GD -8), level on points with 8th-place Orlando City, who host Thursday's Wild Card match with 13 wins to Cincinnati's 12, and one point behind 7th-place Columbus, per the ESPN standings page read at 5:48 a.m. ET Friday, unchanged.

Marshall is 5-4 overall (L1), one of four 5-4 teams listed behind James Madison (8-2) in the Sun Belt East with Georgia Southern, Georgia State and Saturday's visitors App State, per the ESPN standings page read at 5:48 a.m. ET Friday, which carries overall records only and lists Coastal Carolina (3-6) and Old Dominion (3-7) below; Louisiana Tech (7-2, W6) leads the West, where Louisiana went to 7-3 by winning 42-21 at UL Monroe on Thursday night. The basketball team is 2-0 and plays at Purdue tonight.

The Spurs are 10-2 (W10), listed as the Western Conference's 2nd seed, 0.5 behind the Lakers (11-2, W7), who were idle Thursday, per the ESPN NBA standings page read at 5:48 a.m. ET Friday; Minnesota (9-3, W5), who routed Dallas on Thursday night, and Houston (9-3) are 1.5 back, Portland (8-3) is two back, and tonight's visitors Golden State (8-4, L1) are the 6th seed, 2.5 back. Boston (10-2) and Philadelphia (10-3) lead the East.

West Virginia is 5-4 overall (L1), listed 10th of 16 on the ESPN Big 12 standings page read at 5:48 a.m. ET Friday, unchanged; Utah leads at 9-0, Texas Tech is 2nd at 8-1, BYU, Houston and Arizona (all 7-2) follow, and Saturday's visitors Kansas are 3-6 and 16th. The basketball team is 3-0 after Thursday night's win over Mercer and plays Auburn in Las Vegas on Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu forces out Takayasu to stop his run of kinboshi losses at 3 on day 6
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu, back this month from three straight tournaments missed after right-knee surgery in July, charged hard at the tachiai (initial charge), got both arms inside and forced out maegashira (rank-and-file) 3 Takayasu on day 6 at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center on Friday to go to three wins and three losses, ending a three-bout losing streak in which he gave up kinboshi (gold stars, a rank-and-filer's win over a yokozuna) to Fujiryoga, Ura and Fujiseiun; Chunichi Sports reported a fourth straight would have been the first since Miyaginoyama in January 1931. Sports Hochi reported that withdrawal (kyujo) had been discussed and that Hoshoryu telephoned his stablemaster Tatsunami asking to keep fighting; he said afterward he would make no excuses for the losses and wanted to compete to the end, and judge Onoe called it a perfect bout.

briefs.headline: Atamifuji's first loss leaves nobody unbeaten and 9 at one loss after 6 days
briefs.summary: Sekiwake Atamifuji, the only unbeaten man after five days, was forced out by maegashira Asanoyama on day 6 in Fukuoka on Friday, and Kyodo reported that nine rikishi (wrestlers) share the lead at five wins and one loss, among them yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato, who pushed down Hakunofuji in pursuit of a second straight yusho (championship), and ozeki (champion) Kirishima, who forced down Fujiryoga; ozeki Aonishiki threw new komusubi Mitonoumi for a fourth win against two losses, ozeki Kotozakura fell to a second loss on komusubi Yoshinofuji's overarm throw, and sekiwake Fujinokawa pushed out Ura for a second win against four losses. The tournament's final day is Sunday, Nov. 22.

briefs.headline: Cunningham scores 52 as the Pistons outlast the Wizards 144-140 in 2 overtimes
briefs.summary: Cade Cunningham scored a career-high 52 points with 11 assists and no turnovers, the first such line since the NBA began tracking turnovers in the 1977-78 season per OptaSTATS, and Detroit won in Washington on Thursday night after Trae Young's buzzer 3-pointer forced the first overtime and rookie AJ Dybantsa's shot with under a second left forced the second; Ausar Thompson had his first triple-double, 17 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists, Young scored 37 with 14 assists, and Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr had 30 each in Washington's sixth straight loss, per AP. Detroit, with eight wins in 11 games, visits San Antonio on Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Timberwolves rout the Mavericks 133-94 for a 5th straight win
briefs.summary: LaMelo Ball made six 3-pointers for 22 points and a season-high nine assists, Bones Hyland scored 24 off the bench and Minnesota shot 61% in the first half, then outscored Dallas by 19 in the third quarter to lead by as many as 44 in its most lopsided win of the season on Thursday night, a seventh straight over the Mavericks; Zaccharie Risacher scored 22 for Dallas, Cooper Flagg, who had 43 in his last game, was held to 12 and Kyrie Irving to 10 as a three-game winning streak ended, per AP. Minnesota has nine wins in 12 games and sits a game and a half behind the Lakers in the West.

briefs.headline: Daniels' late touchdown pass to Diggs lifts the Commanders over the Giants 24-21
briefs.summary: Jayden Daniels, intercepted twice for the first time this season, hit Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left in East Rutherford, N.J., on Thursday night, and Rasul Douglas intercepted J.J. McCarthy in the final minute to finish it; Daniels was 23 of 33 for 249 yards and three touchdowns, McCarthy threw for a career-high 293 yards and Cam Skattebo ran for two scores for New York, which punted repeatedly after a Jameis Winston sneak for a first down was overturned on review, per AP. Washington moved within two games of the NFC East-leading Giants and holds the tiebreaker after their October tie; the Commanders host the Bengals on Monday, Nov. 23.

briefs.headline: Aho scores twice before a Helsinki crowd as the Hurricanes beat the Kraken 4-1
briefs.summary: Sebastian Aho scored a power-play goal and a one-timer in front of a Finnish crowd, Nikolaj Ehlers had a goal and an assist and fellow Finn Juuso Valimaki also scored as the Stanley Cup champions opened the NHL Global Series at Veikkaus Arena on Thursday, their first game in Helsinki in 16 years, for a seventh win in eight games; Taylor Hall played his 1,000th game, the first player to reach the mark overseas, Brandon Bussi stopped 12 shots and Frederick Gaudreau scored for Seattle, per AP. Carolina is 15-3-2, and the teams meet again in Helsinki on Saturday.

briefs.headline: Jets score the last 6 goals to beat the Stars 8-3 in Dallas
briefs.summary: Mark Scheifele had two goals and an assist, Dawson Mercer scored twice for a second straight game, and Winnipeg turned a one-goal deficit midway through the second period into a fifth straight win with a five-goal second and the game's final six goals on Thursday night; Jake Oettinger, in with the league's fourth-best goals-against average at 1.99, allowed a season-high six on 27 shots and was pulled a minute into the third, and Dallas gave up eight goals for the first time since an 8-2 loss at Winnipeg on Nov. 8, 2016, per AP.

briefs.headline: Memphis blows a 21-point lead, then beats South Florida 52-41 on a 76-yard pass
briefs.summary: Marcus Stokes threw for 313 yards and three touchdowns and ran for two more, and two plays after Nico Gramatica's 38-yard field goal gave the Bulls their first lead with 8:04 left in Tampa on Thursday night, Stokes hit Jemyri Davis for a 76-yard score; J'Mond Tapp's back-to-back sacks ended South Florida's last drive and Jaylin Carter, 109 yards rushing and two touchdowns, capped it from 26 yards, per AP. Memphis is 8-2 and 5-1 in the American Conference and the only FBS team with 50 or more points in two road games this season; Luke Kromenhoek passed for 271 yards and three touchdowns and ran for 146 for South Florida, 6-4.

briefs.headline: Crow-Armstrong and Alvarez take both MVP awards unanimously
briefs.summary: Pete Crow-Armstrong, 24, who hit .280 with 45 home runs and 41 stolen bases and won the Gold and Platinum Gloves for the Cubs, and Yordan Alvarez, 29, who won the AL batting title at .316 with 42 homers, 106 RBIs and an MLB-high 109 walks for Houston a year after a wrist fracture held him to 48 games, each received all 30 first-place votes on Thursday night, the BBWAA announced, the first season in which both MVPs and both Cy Young winners were unanimous; Shohei Ohtani was second in the NL, his sixth straight top-two finish, Brice Turang third, and the Rays' Junior Caminero's second place in the AL ahead of Bobby Witt Jr. is the highest finish by a Tampa Bay player, per ESPN. Alvarez is the second designated hitter to win, after Ohtani.

waters.reading: 80.6 cfs, 1.52 feet at 5:15 a.m., rising on both flow and stage against 43.1 cfs and 1.24 feet in the fetcher's 24-hour comparison.
waters.working: The recession that had the gauge at its lowest of the fall for five mornings ended Thursday: against yesterday's edition reading of 42.0 cfs and 1.23 feet at 5:15 a.m. the river is up 38.6 cfs and 0.29 feet on the day, having nearly doubled. The USGS record held 42.0 until 9:15 a.m. Thursday, then stepped up through 44.2 at 1:15 p.m., 47.6 at 6 p.m., 50.0 at 8:15, 54.9 at 11 p.m., 57.5 at 12:15 a.m., 62.8 at 2, 67.0 at 3, 72.9 at 4 and 77.4 at 4:45 to 80.6 at 5:15, every reading higher than the one before since mid-morning Thursday and the steps coming faster after midnight; the stage climbed one hundredth at a time from 1.23 to 1.52 over the same hours. Eighty cfs at Dyer is still low water on the Williams and the fetcher still calls it prime wading water, but it is rising water, and the difference matters more than the number: a river coming up pushes the trout out of the shallow pocket-water lies toward the seams and the softer edges of the plunge pools, and it carries the first colour in a week. That is a nymph-on-the-seam morning rather than Thursday's long-leader, small-dry problem, a stonefly or a caddis pupa under enough weight to find the bottom of the pools and the inside of the current seams, and with the water up and off-colour a sculpin pattern swung tight to the undercut banks is the first streamer chance the fall has offered; if the rise continues through the day the pools will fish better than the pocket water, and a reader who has waded it at 42 should allow for the push at twice that.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.40 feet at 5 a.m., falling against 24.96 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.4 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Against yesterday's edition reading of 24.99 at 5 a.m. the pool is down 0.59 on the day, and for the first time this week the trace did not make its afternoon round trip: it topped at 25.12 at 6:30 a.m. Thursday, fell through 24.99 at 9, 24.86 at noon and 24.67 at 1:45 p.m., held between 24.65 and 24.76 through the afternoon, then kept going down instead of recovering, 24.58 at 7 p.m., 24.54 at 8, 24.46 at 11, to a low of 24.33 at 12:15 a.m., and has traded between 24.37 and 24.49 since 1 a.m. to read 24.40 at 5. The fetcher reads it as normal pool with ordinary bank access, which it is, but it is the lowest the pool has read this week and 0.6 lower than Monday, so the wing dams and the riprap are showing more rock than they were: shad are the forage and a white or shad-pattern swimbait or a lipless crankbait worked along the exposed face of the wing dams and down the riprap is the pattern on a falling pool, with a jig-and-crawfish on the slack side of the lock wall for the fish that have pulled off the structure as the water dropped. The R.C. Byrd tailwater itself is not gauged; this is the pool side.
waters.source: USGS 03201500 (Ohio River at Point Pleasant); config.SPORTSMAN_WATERS

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.07 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.09 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.1 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Against yesterday's edition reading of 25.9 at 5 a.m. the gauge is up 0.17 on the day, with the whole 24 hours inside half a foot: the trace bottomed at 25.82 at 6:15 a.m. Thursday, climbed through 26.00 at 8:15 and 26.14 at noon to 26.29 at 2:30 p.m., topped at 26.31 at 7:15 p.m., eased through 26.12 at 11:30 p.m. and 26.00 at 3 a.m., rose to 26.16 at 3:45 and read 26.07 at 5. Normal pool, ordinary bank access, and the steadiest of the three gauges this morning while the pool above the dam falls, so the two readings are moving in opposite directions across R.C. Byrd. Below the dam the pattern is the structure the dam makes: skipjack and shad stack in the current below the gates, and a spoon or a heavy jig worked in the churn, or a live skipjack drifted along the current seams off the lock wall, is the hybrid and catfish setup at this stage; the riprap along the Huntington bank fishes a crawfish-colour jig on the slack side where the bank current breaks. The Corps' Byrd tailwater gauge is not available to this pipeline; Huntington is the downstream bracket, 30-odd river miles below the dam, not the tailwater reading.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 4:17 AM at 0.6 ft, high 10:41 AM at 3.9 ft, low 5:08 PM at 0.9 ft, high 10:56 PM at 3.0 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 2:53 AM at 0.7 ft, high 9:35 AM at 4.9 ft, low 4:09 PM at 0.9 ft, high 9:54 PM at 3.4 ft. Water 65.8F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:36 a.m. Moon waxing crescent, 13% illuminated, 3.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 10:41 AM and 10:56 PM in the sound.
waters.working: All four of the sound's events land inside the calendar day, the 4:17 a.m. low behind us at press time, and so do the surf's; the sound lags the surf 84 minutes on the morning low, 66 on the morning high, 59 on the afternoon low and 62 on the evening high, the lows again running further behind than the highs, which is the shallow sound draining slower than it fills. The whole table is 38 to 46 minutes later than Thursday's, the morning range is 3.3 feet against 2.1 feet in the evening, and at 13% and three and a half days old the moon is three days off new and heading for the first-quarter neap, so the current through the inlet is easing each day this week and the evening tide in particular is a soft one. The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report is the monthly one published Nov. 1, 12 days old this morning, and it reads as a pattern, not today's conditions: speckled trout starting to school in the deeper seams and holes of the main creeks in 4 to 16 feet, most in 4 to 8, on live shrimp under a cork or a 3/16-ounce jig head and a small soft plastic, topwater early, with fish to 28 inches reported; scattered red drum inside on cut bait and soft plastics along the oyster and grass banks and 32-inch-plus fish from the piers on the north end; Virginia mullet, spot and thick early-morning bluefish from Jolly Roger Pier, pompano, black drum and croaker from Surf City Pier, and kings, Spanish, false albacore and gray trout off the beach. Tied to today's table: the flood runs from the 4:17 low to the 10:41 high, and the trout bite is the first of the ebb after it, roughly 11 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., a popping cork with live shrimp over the oyster bars at the creek mouths and then the jig and plastic in the 4- to 8-foot holes of the creek channels as the water leaves the grass, with the water at Beaufort down to 65.8F the fish stay in the deeper holes through the afternoon low. Red drum want the last of the fall, which on this table is roughly 2:30 to the 5:08 p.m. low, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges; the 10:56 p.m. high at 3.0 feet is the soft tide of the day, so the flooded-grass window for a weedless gold spoon is short tonight, and the ebb that follows runs under the dock lights toward Saturday's pre-dawn low, the report's small plastics or a suspending twitchbait where the shrimp and finger mullet stack in the light. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel an hour either side of the evening high, and the piers say bottom fishing is better at night. Bluefish are the early-morning fish on the beach behind the bait pods on a metal jig or topwater. Flounder are release only. NWS Wilmington has no active marine, rip current or beach hazards product for Topsail this morning, checked at 5:49 a.m.
